paper_title: Search for light scalar Dark Matter candidate with AURIGA detector
notes: Limit from Fig. 5 (DMplotZOOM.png), the red 'Auriga' curve. The AURIGA resonant-mass detector searches for a scalar 'moduli' DM field. Eq. 4: h = (sqrt(4pi)/M_Pl)(d_me + d_e)Phi, so the electron-mass modulus d_me and the EM-gauge (fine-structure) modulus d_e enter identically and the single red curve is the 95% C.L. upper limit for BOTH couplings (the same numbers apply to ScalarElectron/d_me). The paper's headline abstract number is d_e <= 1e-5 around m_phi = 3.6e-12 eV, so I report the ScalarPhoton/d_e plane; the identical curve bounds d_me. The paper's d_e is defined by alpha -> alpha(1 + d_e*sqrt(4pi*G_N)*Phi) = alpha(1 + d_e*kappa*Phi) with kappa=sqrt(4pi)/M_Pl, i.e. exactly the Damour-Donoghue d_e, so no conversion needed. Curve is a W-shape over the AURIGA sensitive band f=[850,950] Hz (m = h*f = 4.136e-15 eV * f/Hz), spanning m_phi ~ 3.51e-12 to 3.92e-12 eV, with two minima ~3e-6 at the two detector noise minima (~867 and ~930 Hz) and a central peak ~9e-6. Extracted by raster pixel analysis: x calibrated on top f-axis (750 Hz->px252, 1100 Hz->px1085, 119px/50Hz), y on left decades (10^2->y115, 67px/decade). rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3 (Standard Halo Model), stated in abstract. C.L. = 95% via Feldman-Cousins.
